prompt: Should the Claude permission-settings leak block the first Grok worker? `grok inspect --json` reports `~/.claude/settings.local.json` as a loaded permission source even under a fresh isolated GROK_HOME with the full [compat.claude] disable block, and no tested compat key stops it. Answering yes makes T-01 a hard gate on T-07 (the design's current assumption). Answering no lets Grok workers run while T-01 proceeds in parallel, accepting that a worker may be applying the machine owner's personal Claude allow/deny rules.
Which pane mode should Grok workers run in? This decides both the spawn flag and what T-03 captures as monitor markers, so it is cheaper to settle before T-03 than after.
choices: --no-alt-screen (inline) — what the gating spike executed and recommends; more scrollback visible to the surface scrape
--minimal (scrollback-native, small pinned region) — sounds strictly better for scraping but is marked experimental and was never spiked
Default alt-screen / fullscreen — spike-verified to work, but alt-screen teardown drops TUI chrome from the scrape
Let T-03 decide empirically by capturing marker stability under all three and picking the most stable

prompt: Should GrokDriver declare AwaitingInputSignal in v1? The signal shape exists (Notification with notificationType/level) but its vocabulary is uncharacterised, and the capability's contract forbids synthesising the state from a lower-fidelity channel. The design currently omits it (absence disposition Degrade: a Grok worker shows Working/Idle, never a fabricated WaitingForInput) and earns it via T-24. Answering yes would declare it up front and make T-24 a gate instead.

How should the engine tell the app that an Esc-cancelled Grok turn ended? Grok skips the Stop hook on Esc, so the engine's only turn-boundary signal never fires and the slot stays pinned at Working while the worker sits idle at its prompt.
choices: Tail events.jsonl for turn_ended/cancelled — observes the real thing; costs a small new bounded tail, but the path is fully constructible from GROK_HOME + cwd + the Boss-assigned session UUID (the design's recommendation)
Synthesise a turn end engine-side after sending Esc — cheapest, no new transport, but asserts a state it did not observe and is wrong in the optimistic direction if the Esc did not take
Test whether the StopFailure hook covers the interrupt path first, and only build a tail if it does not
